gen-dafont-junegull-gf-armata: Retro and friendly, like letters traced with a marker. Junegull holds that look up top, and Armata's generous letter spacing and open curve endings would let a long stretch of text move along unhurried.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-athiti: Retro, friendly, and stout as cast iron. Junegull's closed, pinched curves lead into Athiti, whose open s lets you see right through, so the two trade tightness for daylight.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-atkinson-hyperleg: Atkinson Hyperlegible has clipped ascenders and capitals, with wide-set terminals on the s. Atkinson Hyperlegible stays open where Junegull closes its letters, and that gap is what keeps the two apart on the page.

Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono spreads its spacing wide like stretched stencil bridges, with counters that breathe and capitals clipped beside the lowercase. Junegull's constant ribbon stroke against that spaced-out body is the draw.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-biryani: Junegull is a retro, friendly display face with closed, pinched curves and cast-iron-tall lowercase. Biryani does the quieter work, with large e eyes and unclogged counters, while the heading simply makes a statement.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-blinker: Stocky, retro and friendly: Junegull pinches its curves shut while Blinker keeps its apertures easily open and its lines uniform. Junegull grabs attention first, and Blinker does the steady reading.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-carrois-gothic: Retro and friendly, Junegull pinches its curves shut and stands its lowercase as tall as cast-iron capitals, a display voice. Carrois Gothic's generous c opening is what sets the two apart.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-carrois-gothic-sc: Carrois Gothic SC keeps a clear opening at the end of every curve, and its capitals barely rise above the lowercase. Against Junegull's closed, pinched letters, that openness is what stands out.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-chivo: Junegull is retro and friendly, its curves pinched shut and its lowercase standing tall like cast-iron capitals. And if Junegull were made small, those pinched curves would crowd, while Chivo keeps daylight through every curve.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-chocolate-classic: Wiry, retro, friendly: Junegull's strokes look like drawn wire, then a broad-nibbed pen takes over. And Chocolate Classical Sans, with a sizable lowercase and curves that never curl shut, would carry paragraphs along comfortably.
